source.description: The attacker-controlled instruction bytes are read/parsed by cs_disasm(Data+1, Size-1, ...); this disassembler parse call is the scored source rather than the libFuzzer callback.
source.value_from: PoC instruction bytes are read/parsed by the Capstone disassembler.; value `Data+1/Size-1`; from `size_t count = cs_disasm(handle, Data+1, Size-1, address, 0, &all_insn);`

sink.description: MSan reports use-of-uninitialized-value when X86_Intel_printInst tests MI->op1_size after the alias/canonical print path.

root_cause.description: The vulnerable Intel printer first calls printAliasInstr and skips canonical printInstruction when an alias is produced; that path can leave MI->op1_size uninitialized before the detail fixup reads it.

tainted_value_origin.code: r = handle->disasm(ud, buffer, size, &mci, &insn_size, offset, handle->getinsn_info);
tainted_value_origin.description: The decoder materializes attacker-controlled instruction state into MCInst mci, including the opcode that triggers the alias/canonical printer behavior.

coarse_trace.summary: Decodes bytes into MCInst and calls the X86 printer.
Alias-first printing can bypass canonical instruction printing and leave operand-size state uninitialized.
MSan origin indicates MI->op1_size can be populated from uninitialized MI->x86opsize in the memory-reference path.
The final detail fixup reads MI->op1_size and triggers MSan.

fine_trace.code: size_t count = cs_disasm(handle, Data+1, Size-1, address, 0, &all_insn);
fine_trace.note: Scored source: cs_disasm reads/parses attacker-controlled instruction bytes into Capstone decoding.

fine_trace.code: r = handle->disasm(ud, buffer, size, &mci, &insn_size, offset, handle->getinsn_info);
fine_trace.note: Decoded opcode/operand state in MCInst is controlled by the input bytes.
The decoded X86 instruction is passed to X86_Intel_printInst.
If printAliasInstr returns an alias mnemonic, the old code skips X86_lockrep and printInstruction. That bypass can leave operand-size state such as MI->op1_size unset before the detail fixup.
MSan origin stack points here as an uninitialized value propagation site for operand-size state.
MSan crash_location reports use of the uninitialized MI->op1_size value here.
